name: Example Faxworth Office Machines (fictional)
summary: A fictional maker of an old type of office machine. Revenue falls every year, profit is shrinking faster, and the dividend was cut. It looks cheap on P/E, and may be cheap for a reason.
assumptions: All figures are fictional and in millions of USD, except the share price. The same tax rate (25% of pre-tax profit), tax rules and accounting apply to every company. No one-off items, share issues or buybacks. Ratios use Year 3 and the current share price. Simulated for learning; not a real firm.
notes: Revenue fell from 500 to 370 million in two years as customers move to newer products. Net income fell by more than half.
The P/E of 5 uses Year 3 earnings. If earnings keep falling, next year's P/E at the same price would be higher, so the low number may not stay low.
The dividend was cut from 30 to 10 million. A high dividend yield based on past payments can disappear.
Debt of 150 million stays the same while profit shrinks, so the interest bill takes a bigger share of operating profit each year.
